theater: 山東平原郡安德縣一帶

battle.name: 李德逸起義
battle.theater: 山東平原郡安德縣一帶
battle.brief: 大業九年（613）正月，平原郡安德縣人李德逸聚眾數萬，沿用劉霸道「阿舅」名號起事，劫掠山東郡縣，郡兵不能制；隋廷正傾師東征高句麗，山東丁役最重。卡面的秦弩屬戰國末至漢初工藝，與本役相隔八百餘年，不在現場；隋軍與起義方真正上手的仍是蹶張弩、步弩與守城床弩，正合弩機存力、以守代攻的老路數。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 大業九年（613）正月起事於山東的這場戰爭，交戰雙方的組織形態極不對稱。起義一方是李德逸在平原郡安德縣聚起的鄉里武裝，《北史》記其聚眾數萬，數萬之眾多由逃戶、亡命、罷役歸鄉的丁男以及附於各路散兵者組成，既無固定編制，也無正式軍號與旗幟，領袖只以名號相呼：《北史》稱其眾為「阿舅賊」，此號承自渤海郡先起事的劉霸道，劉氏眾散之後李德逸沿用不變。山東平原一帶地形開闊，無險可守，這支部眾便以郡縣為目標、以劫掠為生，流動性極強。隋廷一方則是典型的州郡防守體系：地方常備武力為郡兵與縣兵，戶數少、裝備劣，多由鄉里壯丁臨時編組，平日守城而已；中央可調的正軍是自京師宿衛、各地府兵與州郡鎮兵中抽調的行軍，加上一批屢次平叛的老將，例如同期在山東追剿諸股起義的虎賲郎將張須陀。指揮系統是郡守郡丞、州刺史州長史逐級上報，行軍總管或行軍長史臨軍統制，兵符與調兵文書仍能運作，但府兵制已名存實亡，募兵與鄉兵混編，使各部戰力與指揮關係都極為鬆散。第三方也並非局外人：北方有突厥壓境，東邊高句麗是隋廷三次東征的對手，江淮與江南同時有朱燮、汪文進等人舉事，河北則有竇建德、郝元貞等部在同年並起。李德逸這支力量正是在這樣的背景下，從隋廷視線的縫隙裡迅速膨脹。
countriesEn: This war broke out in Shandong in the first month of the ninth year of the Daye era (613), and the two sides were organised in radically different ways. The rebel side was a local armed band gathered by Li Deyi in Anding county of Pingyuan commandery. The Bei Shi records that he gathered tens of thousands of men, and most of them were runaways from the tax registers, men in flight, conscripts discharged and drifted home, and stragglers attached to the various wandering bands. There was no regular establishment, no formal army title and no banners; the leader was known only by a nickname. The Bei Shi calls the band the A-Jiu bandits, a designation inherited from Liu Bodang, who had risen earlier in Bohai commandery: once Liu's followers dispersed, Li Deyi kept the same name. The plains of Shandong are open and offer no natural defensive ground, so this force made the commandery and county seats its targets and lived off plunder, moving with great fluidity. On the Sui side stood the typical commandery-and-county defence system. The permanent local strength was the commandery soldiers and the county soldiers, few in number and poorly equipped, mostly ad hoc levies of local able-bodied men who were meant for nothing more than holding a walled town. The regular troops the court could move were detachments drawn from the metropolitan guards, the regional fu-bing and the standing garrisons of the prefectures, reinforced by a handful of experienced commanders such as Zhang Xutuo, the Tiger Guard lieutenant, who chased the rebel bands through Shandong in these same years. The chain of command ran from the commandery governor and his assistant up through the prefect, with a campaign commander or campaign director taking charge in the field; military tally tallies and written orders still functioned, but the fu-bing system had become nominal, and the mixture of recruited and local troops left every unit's fighting quality and its ties of command extremely loose. The third parties were not bystanders either: the Turks pressed from the north, Goguryeo to the east was the opponent of the Sui's three campaigns, in the Yangzi and the Jiangnan there were simultaneous risings by Zhu Xie, Wang Wenjin and others, and in Hebei Dou Jiande, Hao Yuanzhen and their bands rose in the same year. Li Deyi's force grew precisely in such a setting, swelling quickly in the gaps of the court's attention.
people: 大業九年正月二十，聚眾於平原郡安德縣、率眾劫掠山東的，正是李德逸本人。史籍關於他的記載極少，《北史》只留下數十字的斷片：他是平原郡安德縣人，隋末民變中平原起義的領袖，於大業九年正月二十聚眾數萬，稱「阿舅賊」，劫掠山東；除姓名、籍貫與事蹟之外，他的出身、起義前的身份、以及事後的下落都沒有留下記錄。可以確定的是，他並非職業將領，而是憑地方鄉里的人脈與對時局的判斷，在郡兵無力防守的空白地帶一舉聚起數萬之眾。他也不是山東最早起事者：渤海郡人劉霸道早已聚眾作亂，同樣以「阿舅」為號劫掠郡縣；農民起義聚散無常，劉氏之眾散去之後，李德逸接手沿用同一名號，把散而復聚的鄉民重新編在「阿舅」旗號之下。這說明當時山東河北一帶的武裝抗爭已有可沿用的號召傳統，起義者爭的是鄉里的信任，而不是城池的險固。官軍方面，隋煬帝楊廣面對的是一個四處起火的全局面：大業八年冬第三次征高句麗，傾天下的兵與糧往遼東，士卒逃還、疫癘與糧秣不接相繼而來，山東、河北正是運糧與徵丁的腹地，怨氣最重。同期在山東的官軍主將是虎賲郎將張須陀，他屢次在齊郡、北海一帶追擊王薄、張保周等股，傳記稱其常以少數精兵擊破數萬之眾；史書並未記載他與李德逸有正面交鋒，但正因官軍精銳被各股分散、主力遠在遼東與江南，李德逸得以在郡縣之間來回周旋。同年八月太原李淵起兵，關中方向再開新戰場，隋廷更無餘力回頭收拾山東。
peopleEn: The man who gathered a crowd in Anding county of Pingyuan commandery on the twentieth day of the first month of the ninth year of Daye and led it in plundering Shandong was Li Deyi himself. Very little is recorded about him; the Bei Shi preserves only a few dozen characters: he was a native of Anding county in Pingyuan commandery, and the leader of the Pingyuan rising among the late-Sui rebellions; in the first month of the ninth year of Daye he gathered tens of thousands of men, called them the A-Jiu bandits, and raided Shandong. Beyond his name, his home county and this single episode, nothing is known about his origins, his status before the rising, or his fate afterwards. What can be established is that he was not a professional soldier: he relied on local ties in the countryside and on a reading of the moment to raise tens of thousands of men in a stretch of countryside where the commandery troops were too few to hold the ground. Nor was he the first to rise in Shandong. Liu Bodang of Bohai commandery had already taken to the field, raiding commanderies and counties under the same A-Jiu name; such risings gathered and dispersed unpredictably, and when Liu's followers melted away, Li Deyi took over the same designation and folded the re-gathered villagers once again under that banner. This shows that armed resistance in the Shandong-Hebei region already had a usable tradition of rallying cries: what the insurgents were contesting was the trust of the countryside, not the security of a walled city. On the government side, Emperor Yang of Sui faced fires burning in every quarter. In the winter of the eighth year of Daye the third campaign against Goguryeo sent the empire's soldiers and grain north to Liaodong, and troops deserting, epidemics and a collapsing supply line followed one another; Shandong and Hebei, the rear areas through which the grain and the conscripts passed, were the most resentful of all. The Sui commander in Shandong at the time was Zhang Xutuo, lieutenant of the Tiger Guard, who repeatedly hunted Wang Bo, Zhang Baozhou and similar bands around the Qi and Beihai regions, and whose biography credits him with breaking tens of thousands with only a small body of picked troops. No source records a direct engagement between him and Li Deyi; but precisely because the Sui's best troops were scattered among several bands and the main body lay far away in Liaodong and the Jiangnan, Li Deyi was able to move back and forth between commanderies and counties. In the eighth month of the same year Li Yuan rose at Taiyuan, opening a further front in the Guanzhong direction, and the court had even less strength left with which to deal with Shandong.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是秦弩，屬戰國末至漢初的工藝：木製弩臂，銅或鐵製弩機，含郭、機牙、懸機與望山，矢以竹木為桿、骨為鏃。弩的關鍵在於把拉力存進弩機，射手不必像弓手那樣在放箭的一瞬間拉開整條臂，於是可以在城牆上、盾後、馬背上反覆使用，射速與精度都勝過拉弓；缺點是張弦費力、體積笨重，連發不易，因此漢家給善射弩者專設材官之職，按郡國每年考核選拔，並依制配發弩具。卡面那句「守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外」，說的正是弩最本分的位置：不是用來正面決勝，而是用來把攀城者釘在牆外。不過要分清卡面與現場——秦弩的形制距離大業九年的山東已有八百餘年，本役並無秦弩出土或列入戰記，隋人也不會用秦弩。隋唐之際真正上手的弩是蹶張弩，以腳踏上弩機、借全身之力張弦，適合列陣齊發；步騎通用的臂弓配在披甲步兵與輕騎手上；守城方向另有可疊置的床弩與積弩一類的機關，配合矢石與投石，專門壓制填壕、蟻附的隊列。起義一方多為步行鄉民，馬匹與弩具都極缺乏，武器以弓箭、繩索、長矛與朴刀為主，遇城只能靠人梯、火攻與內應，或避實擊虛、專劫糧車與府庫。兩軍共通的裝備還包括環首刀、鐵矛與戟，皮甲與札甲，騎兵用長槊，官軍另有精騎、戰馬與運糧車隊；黃河下游的舟楫與驛道負責調兵運糧，山東是隋朝供應遼東前線的糧源之一，糧道的安危往往比城池本身更能決定戰局。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a Qin crossbow, a design of the late Warring States and early Han: a wooden bow arm with a bronze or iron lock mechanism comprising the bow casing, the trigger, the trigger bar and the sight, fired with arrows of bamboo or wood shaft and bone head. The whole point of the crossbow is that the pull is stored in the lock, so the shooter does not have to draw the full length of the arm at the instant of release as an archer must; it can therefore be used again and again from a wall, from behind a shield or on horseback, and it out-ranges and out-volleys the bow in both rate and accuracy. Its drawbacks are the effort of spanning and its bulk, which make rapid repetition awkward, so the Han gave skilled crossbowmen their own post as cail guan, selected each year by examination in the commanderies and issued crossbows to them according to regulation. The card's remark that the defenders use it to hold the attackers outside the wall describes the crossbow's proper station: not the weapon of decision in the open field, but the weapon that pins climbers to the face of the wall. The card and the battlefield must nevertheless be kept apart. The Qin crossbow was more than eight hundred years out of date in Li Deyi's Shandong, and no Qin crossbow is listed in the fighting record of this campaign; the Sui did not use such things. The crossbows actually handled in the Sui and Tang were the foot-spanned type (chuang zhang), spanned by stamping on the lock and using the weight of the body, suitable for massed volleys; the ordinary bow was carried by armoured foot and light horse; and for the defence of walls there were stacked bed-crossbows and the like, worked with arrows, stones and traction engines, deployed specifically against troops filling ditches and scaling the ramparts. The insurgents were for the most part foot-bound villagers with almost no horses and almost no crossbows, armed with bows, rope, long spears and plain swords; before a walled town they could only rely on human ladders, fire and insiders, or else strike where the garrison was weak and go for the grain carts and the granaries. Equipment common to both sides included ring-pommel swords, iron spears and halberds, leather and lamellar armour, long lances for the cavalry; the Sui additionally had picked horse, war ponies and baggage trains, while the fleets and the post roads of the lower Yellow River moved troops and grain, for Shandong was one of the grain sources feeding the Liaodong front. The safety of that grain line often mattered more to the outcome than the walled cities themselves.
tactics: 起義方的戰術核心是流動與規避。李德逸眾多不據城、不守壘，也不與官軍主力正面硬撼；他們憑藉熟悉鄉里道路、熟悉各縣糧秣儲藏的優勢，在郡縣之間轉移，趁郡兵空虛或守將赴鄰郡救援時劫掠府庫、糧倉與驛傳，奪得騎兵賴以奔馳的馬匹後立刻散入鄉野。史書以「聚散無常」形容這類武裝：號令鬆散，遇大股官軍即解散歸戶，兵散後再聚，所以官軍即使斬獲甚眾，也難以一戰畢其功。劫掠而無城池憑依，也意味著起義方缺乏攻城器械與持續攻堅的能力，戰術上限被壓在襲擾與破壞這一級。官軍這邊的應對是收縮與分討：郡兵守城、縣兵守土，閉門拒敵，以烽火傳警，再由州郡彙報朝廷，遣行軍分道討平。守城的骨幹是弩手，登上城垛、藏入射孔之後，張弦、上矢、瞄準、發射，一發之後再上下一發，以居高臨下的射距與機括的穩定性持續壓制攀城者；配合矢石、投石與撞車，使攻城隊伍的填壕與蟻附被迫在弩矢之下進行。真正追擊潰散之眾的，是各軍抽調的精騎，官軍的戰術是先用弩與城牆把起義者釘在城下或道路上，再以騎兵衝其不整之陣；張須陀能在山東追著幾股起義打，靠的正是這樣的組合。地形也在其中：黃河下游在隋代多經平原郡一帶，河道寬緩、渡口與淺灘相間，水淺時可涉、盛水時靠舟楫，春冬水枯冰結，渡口成天然橋梁，兵糧可以快速通過，也讓郡縣之間的距離變短。起義方熟悉這些渡口與泥濘道路，官軍的舟車與騎兵反而受制於季節。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the insurgents was mobility and evasion. Li Deyi's men as a rule neither occupied cities nor held entrenched camps, and they did not try to stand and fight the main body of the Sui army; drawing on their familiarity with the roads of the countryside and with where each county stored its grain and stores, they shifted from commandery to commandery, and struck at granaries, depots and the post service while the commandery troops were thin or while the local commander was away helping a neighbouring prefecture, seizing the horses on which the government cavalry depended and then vanishing back into the villages. The histories describe such bands as gathering and dispersing unpredictably: discipline was loose, and faced with a large Sui force they dissolved into their households, only to re-form later, so that even a government army taking heavy casualties could not finish them in a single battle. Living by plunder without a walled base also meant that the insurgents lacked siege machines and the capacity to sustain an assault, and their tactical ceiling was fixed at the level of harassment and destruction. The Sui answer was contraction and separate campaigns: commandery soldiers holding towns, county soldiers holding the ground, doors shut against the enemy, beacons lit to pass the warning along, reports carried up through the prefectures to the court, and campaign columns dispatched by separate routes to suppress each band. The backbone of the defence was the crossbowman, who climbed the parapet, sheltered behind the firing aperture, spanned the bow, nocked, aimed and loosed, then re-spanned and fired again; from above, with a stable lock, this kept the scaling parties under continuous fire, and with arrows, stones and battering rams it forced the attackers to fill ditches and climb beneath the bolts. It was the picked horse that actually ran down the broken remnants: the Sui method was to pin the insurgents against the walls or on the roads with crossbows and ramparts, and then charge them with cavalry while their order was broken. That combination was what allowed Zhang Xutuo to hunt several bands across Shandong. Terrain played its part as well. In Sui times the lower Yellow River ran through the region of Pingyuan commandery, broad and slow, with fords and shallows alternating; it could be waded when shallow and used by boat when full, and in the dry winter and spring the frozen water at the fords made natural bridges, so that troops and grain moved quickly and the distance between one commandery seat and the next was shortened. The insurgents knew these fords and the muddy roads intimately; the court wagons and cavalry were in the end at the mercy of the season.
data: 關於這場戰爭能查到的數字非常有限，以下幾項有史籍依據，其餘只能存疑。其一，時間：《北史》記大業九年正月二十李德逸聚眾起事，換成公曆約在公元613年初，距離大業八年冬隋軍第三次大舉東征高句麗出發，僅數月之隔。其二，兵力：起義方聚眾數萬，此數為史書約數，諸書不一，多指裹挾鄉民、隨聚隨散之眾，並非可以常規作戰的戰鬥兵員；先起事的劉霸道同樣以數萬計。官軍方面，隋廷在山東可調的正軍是各路分道討平的偏師，郡兵與縣兵的編制史無明文，一般只在數百至數千之間，戰力遠遜於京師宿衛；作對照，大業八年征高句麗時全國調動之兵逾百萬，其中山東一地只是徵發的後方之一，比例極小。其三，斬獲與戰果：官軍在山東追剿王薄、張保周等股，傳記多稱斬首以萬計，具體數字各書不一；李德逸部眾的損失與存亡，史料只說「郡兵不能制」與其後眾散，沒有留下可以核對的數目。其四，距離與補給：安德縣在平原郡治所，東距渤海郡治陽鳥約二百餘里，南至齊州歷城約二百里，北越黃河通往渤海郡諸縣，西去幽州涿郡的遼東前線近六百里。糧食沿黃河與濟水下游的水路、驛道北運，民夫由山東一路徵發，運糧隊伍常成起義方襲擊的目標。其五，弩具與射手：漢制每郡每年考核選拔材官、按弩具數量配發，隋代沿襲漢唐以來郡國備弩的傳統，但各郡實際弩數與射手人數無明文記載，此處只能說明弩在守城編制中的固定位置，不可據以推算確數。
dataEn: Very few figures survive for this war; the following items rest on textual authority, and everything else must remain conjectural. First, the date: the Bei Shi places the rising on the twentieth day of the first month of the ninth year of Daye, which in the Gregorian calendar falls in the early part of 613 CE, only a few months after the Sui armies set out on their third great campaign against Goguryeo in the winter of the eighth year of Daye. Second, numbers of troops: the insurgents are recorded as tens of thousands, a round figure that varies from book to book and mostly counts villagers drawn along with the band, coming and going with it, rather than a body of men who could be fought in the field; Liu Bodang, who rose earlier, is likewise counted in tens of thousands. On the government side, the regular troops the court could move in Shandong were the detached columns sent out by separate routes, while the establishment of the commandery and county soldiers is nowhere recorded in detail and was probably in the range of several hundred to a few thousand, far below the metropolitan guards; for comparison, the third campaign against Goguryeo mobilised more than a million men across the empire, of which Shandong was only one of the rear areas of conscription, a very small share. Third, losses and results: in the pursuit of Wang Bo, Zhang Baozhou and the other bands in Shandong the official accounts speak of heads taken in the tens of thousands, with the precise numbers differing from book to book; for Li Deyi's own band the record contains only the statement that the commandery soldiers could not hold and that the multitude later dispersed, leaving no figure that can be checked. Fourth, distances and supply: Anding county lay at the seat of Pingyuan commandery, about two hundred and some li east of the seat of Bohai commandery at Yangniao, about two hundred li south of the prefecture seat of Qizhou at Licheng, north across the Yellow River towards the counties of Bohai, and rather less than six hundred li from Youzhou and Zhuo commandery on the Liaodong front. Grain moved north by water and by post road along the lower Yellow River and the lower Ji, with corvée labourers conscripted along the way in Shandong, and grain convoys were a standing target for the insurgents. Fifth, crossbows and crossbowmen: Han regulations had each commandery examine and select cail guan every year and issue crossbows according to the numbers enrolled, and the Sui inherited the Han and Tang practice of keeping crossbows in the commanderies, but the actual number of crossbows and of crossbowmen in each commandery is nowhere recorded; the point can only be made that the crossbow held a fixed place in the defence establishment, not that any quantity can be computed from it.
cause: 大業九年正月李德逸在平原郡安德縣聚眾，不是孤立事件，而是隋朝第三次征高句麗的戰敗與全國徭役崩潰在山東的一次爆發。直接導火線在一年之前。大業八年（612）冬，隋煬帝以傾國之兵第三次東征高句麗，陸軍自涿郡北進，糧道自黃河下游與永濟渠北運，山東、河北正是徵丁、徵糧與轉運的腹地。戰役未竟而前線崩潰，士卒逃散，屍骨暴露於野，糧秣與器械大量耗損而無以為繼，被徵發的民夫與丁壯大量滯留或逃亡。這種代價，最後都壓在山東的鄉里頭上。更深一層是結構性的消耗：隋朝自開皇以來租調力役並行，戶口雖增而丁役愈重；大業年間三征高句麗、兩巡江都，營造東都與洛陽，兵役、漕運、雜供同時加急，山東與江南都是重災區。地方官員催科之外還要維持龐大的郡兵與轉運，老百姓既不能留鄉又無力遠行，於是出現大批游離於戶籍之外的亡命之民，一旦有人登高一呼，他們的聚集不需要複雜的組織，只需要一個名號。劉霸道的先例提供了號召的樣板：渤海郡眾以「阿舅」相稱，聚散無常，其眾既散，李德逸便沿用同一名號在平原郡重新聚起數萬之眾。同一年，齊郡王薄在長白山、渤海郡竇建德、平原郝元貞、江淮朱燮與汪文進各自舉事，山東河北一帶已呈多點爆發之勢。對隋廷而言，山東的問題從來不是某一路起義，而是整個郡縣系統在同一時間失去了應付能力。諸家史書對起義的直接起因記載有限，但大業九年的時間點與規模都指向同一個解釋：連續的東征把國家的最後一點儲備耗盡，任何一個火星都足以點燃山東。
causeEn: The gathering of men by Li Deyi at Anding county in Pingyuan commandery in the first month of the ninth year of Daye was not an isolated event; it was an eruption in Shandong of the defeat of the Sui's third campaign against Goguryeo and of the collapse of labour service across the empire. The immediate trigger lay a year earlier. In the winter of the eighth year of Daye (612) Emperor Yang of Sui sent the bulk of the empire's army against Goguryeo for the third time, the land route advancing from Zhuo commandery and the grain route running north along the lower Yellow River and the Yongji Canal, with Shandong and Hebei serving as the rear country from which the conscripts, the grain and the transport were drawn. The campaign broke down before it was finished: soldiers fled, bodies were left unburied in the open, grain and equipment were consumed with nothing to replace them, and a great many of the corvée labourers and conscripts never came home or went into flight. That reckoning was ultimately paid by the villages of Shandong. Deeper down lay a structural exhaustion. Since the Kaihuang era the Sui had run grain tax and labour service together: the registered population grew even as the burden of service grew heavier; in the years of Daye the third Goguryeo campaign, the two imperial tours of Jiangdu, the building of the eastern and western capitals, military service, river transport and miscellaneous levies all came due at once, and Shandong and the Jiangnan were the worst affected. Local officials, besides collecting the taxes, had to maintain large commandery garrisons and the transport system; the common people could neither stay at home nor afford the journey, and so great numbers of them floated free of the registers. Once somebody raised a standard, such men needed no elaborate organisation to assemble; all they needed was a name. Liu Bodang had provided the model: the multitude in Bohai commandery called itself A-Jiu, it gathered and scattered unpredictably, and when it dispersed Li Deyi simply reused the same name and raised tens of thousands again in Pingyuan commandery. In that same year Wang Bo rose at Changbai in Qi commandery, Dou Jiande in Bohai, Hao Yuanzhen in Pingyuan, and Zhu Xie and Wang Wenjin in the Yangzi and the Jiangnan, so that Shandong and Hebei were already breaking out in many places at once. For the court the problem in Shandong was never a single rising but the failure of the entire commandery and county system to cope at one and the same time. The direct occasion is thinly recorded in the histories, but both the timing and the scale of the ninth year of Daye point to the same explanation: the repeated eastern campaigns had spent the last of the state's reserves, and in that condition any single spark was enough to set Shandong alight.
impact: 李德逸起義本身規模有限、記載極簡，但它落在隋末崩解的關鍵位置上，後果並不有限。第一，山東的郡縣秩序迅速失效。郡兵不能制、縣兵不足守，起義眾得以在郡縣間流動劫掠，隋廷在山東的實際控制只剩下有官軍駐紮的城池與主要驛道；地方豪強與鄉里大姓不得不各自武裝自保，山東社會從郡縣制迅速退回以塢堡、寨圍為核心的狀態。第二，官軍被迫多線分兵，導致每一線都缺乏足以掃平股匪的兵力。派往山東的討平軍要同時應付王薄、張保周、李德逸、郝元貞等數股，反覆用兵而未能畢其功；而同年十月隋煬帝下詔罷兵、撤還前線，把大軍撤回關中與河南，遼東戰線自此放棄，此舉使山東的民變更加無所牽制，數年之後河北與山東成了竇建德、劉黑闥得以經營的真空地帶。第三，加速了隋朝在中原的崩解與權力真空的形成。613年之內，太原有李淵起兵，河北有竇建德，江南有高智慧，淮南有杜彥威，關中與河東的戰線互相不能支援；隋朝在山東既不能守也無法壓，兵源與財源兩端同時枯竭，五年之後隋室傾覆，李唐於618年建立，李世民、王世充、竇建德、劉黑闥在山東河北的爭奪遂成為隋唐之際最激烈的戰場之一。第四，在軍事制度上，這場戰爭再次印證了府兵制的崩壞：隋朝無法以制度化的兵源迅速平叛，募兵與鄉兵的混雜編組成為唯一可行的辦法，卻又直接導致兵將不相習、調度失靈的惡果；而守城依賴弩與城牆的傳統也說明，在缺乏攻城器械與攻堅能力的起義方面前，城防仍是最有效也最脆弱的防線。第五，就卡面這件兵器而言，秦弩所代表的「以守制攻」邏輯在隋末唐初仍然通用：弩手在城頭、井欄與塹壕之後，把進攻者壓在城外；唐初的城防編制與後來的守城器械，都沿著同一條技術路線展開。
impactEn: Li Deyi's rising was limited in scale and very thinly recorded, but it fell at a critical hinge of the late-Sui collapse, and its consequences were not limited. First, the administrative order of Shandong failed quickly. The commandery soldiers could not hold and the county soldiers were too few, so the insurgents moved freely from commandery to commandery plundering, and the court's actual control over Shandong came down to the towns garrisoned by regular troops and the main post roads; local magnates and great families had to arm and protect themselves, and Shandong society fell back rapidly from the commandery-and-county system onto a pattern of walled villages and stockades. Second, the government was forced to divide its forces along several lines, and no single line then had the strength to sweep the bands away. The column sent to suppress Shandong had to deal at once with Wang Bo, Zhang Baozhou, Li Deyi and Hao Yuanzhen, and was used over and over without finishing any of them; then in the tenth month of the same year Emperor Yang ordered the armies stood down and the front withdrawn, pulling the troops back to Guanzhong and the Yellow River valley and abandoning the Liaodong line for good. From then on the risings in Shandong faced no restraint at all, and within a few years Hebei and Shandong became the empty ground in which Dou Jiande and Liu Heitao were able to build. Third, the rising hastened the Sui's dissolution in the plains and the formation of a vacuum of power. Within the single year 613 there was Li Yuan at Taiyuan, Dou Jiande in Hebei, Gao Zhihui in the Jiangnan and Du Yanwei in the Huai, and the fronts in Guanzhong and Hedong could not support one another. The Sui could neither hold Shandong nor crush it, and both its manpower and its revenue were exhausted at once; five years later the dynasty fell and the Tang was founded in 618, and the struggle of Li Shimin, Wang Shichong, Dou Jiande and Liu Heitao over Shandong and Hebei became one of the fiercest theatres of the Sui-Tang transition. Fourth, in military-administrative terms the rising confirmed the collapse of the fu-bing system: the Sui could not raise troops quickly enough to pacify the country through institutional levies, and the only workable expedient was a mixture of recruited and local soldiers, which in turn produced troops and commanders who did not know one another and an apparatus of command that broke down. At the same time, the reliance of the defence on the crossbow and the wall shows that against insurgents who possessed neither siege engines nor the capacity to sustain an assault, the city defences remained both the most effective and the most fragile of barriers. Fifth, as far as the weapon on the card is concerned, the Qin crossbow embodied a logic of defence by holding the attacker off that remained in use in the late Sui and early Tang: crossbowmen behind the parapet, behind the wells and behind the ditches pressed the assaulting party against the outside of the wall, and the Tang's city defence establishment and its later siege equipment developed along the same technical line.
result: 這場戰爭沒有留下會戰的記載，結果只能從零星線索拼出輪廓。就眼前的戰事而言：李德逸於大業九年正月二十在平原郡安德縣聚眾數萬，稱「阿舅賊」，劫掠山東，郡兵不能制，說明其初期是成功的——至少在郡縣防守上取得了實際突破。隋廷隨後分道遣將討平，張須陀等部在山東追剿諸股；至大業十年前後，王薄、張保周等相繼被平，李德逸這一支也隨之潰散，其本人下落不明。《北史》與《隋書》關於這位起義領袖不過數十字，既未記載他被擒或被斬，也未記載他另建政權，事實上他很可能在大業九年之內就已散伙，重歸鄉里或流亡他處，諸說並存。就全局而言，隋朝在山東的平叛並沒有成功。以後數年，河北的竇建德勢力迅速膨脹，於619年稱帝建夏，控制的正是當年被李德逸這類起義者擾亂過的河北與山東郡縣；621年竇建德敗於虎牢關後，唐朝再用數年平定山東，最終由李世民、李世勣把山東收入版圖。李德逸的名字隨著隋末亂世的第一波民變沉入史冊深處，他所留下的卻是一個時代的註腳：當一個王朝把最後的儲備耗在遼東戰場上，山東的郡兵就再也擋不住幾萬個拿著繩索與長矛的鄉民。從兵器與戰術的角度看，這場戰爭留下的是一條清楚的教訓——當攻城方缺乏雲梯、撞車與足以遮蔽的甲兵時，守方的弩手與城牆就是唯一的依靠；而當守方連郡兵都湊不齊時，再好的弩也只不過是把防守的時間從幾天拖成幾個月。隋末唐初的城防技術，正是從這樣的教訓裡一寸寸累積起來的。
resultEn: This war left no record of a pitched battle, and its outcome can only be pieced together from scattered clues. As to the fighting itself: on the twentieth day of the first month of the ninth year of Daye Li Deyi gathered tens of thousands at Anding county in Pingyuan commandery, called them the A-Jiu bandits and raided Shandong; the commandery soldiers could not hold him, which means that his opening was successful, at least in the sense that he achieved a real breach in the county and commandery defences. The court then dispatched separate columns to suppress the bands, and units such as Zhang Xutuo's hunted the insurgents across Shandong; by around the tenth year of Daye Wang Bo, Zhang Baozhou and the others were being suppressed one after another, and Li Deyi's band fell apart with them, its leader's fate unknown. The Bei Shi and the Su Shu give this rebel leader no more than a few dozen characters, recording neither his capture nor his death, nor any polity he founded; in all likelihood he had already broken up within the ninth year of Daye, either going home or drifting away, and the accounts differ. In wider terms, the Sui's suppression of Shandong did not succeed. Within a few years Dou Jiande's power in Hebei swelled rapidly and in 619 he proclaimed himself emperor and founded the Xia state, ruling precisely over the Hebei and Shandong commanderies that men like Li Deyi had disturbed; after Dou Jiande's defeat at Hulao Pass in 621 the Tang spent further years pacifying Shandong, and it was Li Shimin and Li Shiji who finally brought the region into the empire. Li Deyi's name sank deep into the early waves of late-Sui rebellion, but what he left behind was a footnote on an era: once a dynasty had spent its last reserves on a battlefield in Liaodong, the commandery soldiers of Shandong could no longer hold back tens of thousands of villagers carrying rope and long spears. In terms of weapons and tactics, the war left a plain lesson — when the attacker lacks ladders, battering rams and armour heavy enough to cover the assault, the defenders' crossbowmen and ramparts are the only reliance; and when the defenders cannot even muster their commandery soldiers, the best crossbow in the world only buys a few more days instead of a few months. The siegecraft of the late Sui and early Tang was built up inch by inch out of lessons of exactly this kind.
